text:
Zara: quick follow-up from the cross-shard meeting — want to capture the token-decay + coordination idea
Ben: nice, what's the core problem again?
Zara: soft tokens issued on one shard can be spammed to create apparent local occupancy, hurting global fairness
Kofi: right. we saw tenants open soft tokens across 3 shards and push others out of confirmed slots
Dana: proposed fix: make soft tokens globally bounded via a lightweight coordination shard that maintains soft_counts per-tenant
Ben: coordination shard = single source of truth? worried about latency on hot paths
Zara: not hot path. the idea: token issue checks a cached soft_quota locally; local cache syncs with coord shard every 200ms or on delta
Kofi: so local fast-path reads cache, but long-running sync avoids per-request RPC. prefix only used for gating, not billing
Dana: and we add decay schedule centrally: soft_weight decreases by factor every T seconds, stored in coord shard ledger
Ben: how do we handle races when a local cache allows a token but coord shard is already at limit? rollback rare but possible
Zara: plan: optimistic issue locally, emit async reconcile event; if reconcile fails, mark token_revoked and evict if not yet confirmed
Kofi: token_revoked should be idempotent and cheap; do not promote revoked tokens to hard credits in any case
Dana: rollback policy: if revoked after promotion, count as eviction and increment eviction_backoff; avoid revoking promoted tokens unless severe
Ben: need clear invariants: promotion only when local and coord agree (coord.confirm_count + local.pending_promotions <= global_limit)
Zara: agree. pseudo: \n```\n# local fast-path\nif local_cache.soft_count < local_soft_limit:\n  issue_soft_token()\n  emit async reconcile(token)\n\n# reconcile handler (coord shard)\nif coord.global_soft_count < global_soft_limit:\n  coord.accept(token)\nelse:\n  coord.reject(token)\n```\nKofi: metrics: coord_accept_rate, token_revokes, cross_shard_soft_count, coord_sync_lag
Dana: operationally, run coord shard replicated (n=3) with hot standby; make it partition-tolerant for reads via stale reads
Ben: what about failure modes? if coord shard partitioned, locals should fall back to conservative mode (N_soft_local=1)
Zara: yes fallback: safe-mode reduces speculative soft issuance to avoid gaming and memory blowup
Kofi: long-term thought: replace coord shard with probabilistic counters (CRDT style) to avoid strict sync but still bound global issuance
Dana: CRDT would give eventual consistency but harder to enforce hard limits; might be fine for best-effort soft tokens
Ben: also consider per-tenant per-region quotas to reduce cross-region thrash and keep cache coherence simple
Zara: rollout plan: RFC -> small canary with coord-shard read-only mode (logs only) -> experimental enforcement on 2 low-risk tenants -> broader rollout
Kofi: rollback triggers: token_revokes>baseline*2 sustained 10m OR coord_sync_lag>500ms for 5m
Dana: add trace linkage: reservation_id -> coord_event_id -> batch_id -> eviction_id for root-cause
sre-bot: scheduled canary: coord-shard read-only mode on shard-x starting in 10m
deploy-bot: canary queued: shard-x with feature coord_soft_quota=true
Ben: I'll draft the RFC section on invariants and reconcile semantics. include the pseudo and the safe-mode behavior
Zara: thanks. I'll add the telemetry dashboards and tie alerts to the rollback triggers. Ping me for reviews :thumbsup:
